Remove it from here very quickly!

words.gloss: to remove, to take away; to tidy up

lines.trans: Lyova, have you already found my knife?
We have not found it yet, Chef.
Did you definitely look well everywhere?
Yes, we checked everything in the kitchen.
Then continue to look further!
Someone could accidentally leave the knife inside.
For example, someone forgot the knife in the fish.
In the fish? That is impossible, Chef!
I do not know. Look everywhere!
Alright, Chef, we will find everything.
Without the knife we will not be able to work!
Why did you put a dirty box here?
Remove it from here very quickly!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'without' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'everywhere'.

examples.trans: Vanya, the water! There's water everywhere!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'inside'.

examples.trans: There's the same kind of bug inside.

examples.text: Вы его спиртом растёрли? И внутри тоже растёрли?!
examples.trans: You rubbed him with alcohol? And on the inside too?!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dirty').

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'next'.
Secondary conversational sense ('next, go on') (in a list or a story) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'so'.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'box'.

examples.trans: We were putting it into boxes.
A big box was standing on the floor.

examples.text: Шалфей был. Мы его в коробки клали.
examples.trans: It was sage. We were putting it into boxes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('someone') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'пример').

examples.trans: Here, for example, is the boy.
Let's take, for instance, this case.

examples.text: А мы многое что можем сделать. Вот, например, мальчик.
examples.trans: Oh, there's plenty we can do. Here, for example, is the boy.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'impossible' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: This is an entirely impossible situation.
It is impossible to work in such noise.
In the fish? That is impossible, Chef!

meanings.note: end-stressed in all oblique forms: ножа, ножом

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
There is a sharp knife on the table.

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'оставлять'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to keep, to save') (оставь мне кусок = save me a piece) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I won't leave him on his own.

examples.text: Вика, ну он одинокий. Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: Vika, come on, he's all alone. I can't just leave him on his own.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'from here'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'ставить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to install') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Put your foot on the bed.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to continue', paired with 'продолжить'.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: а вы случайно не...? = are you by any chance...?
Secondary conversational sense ('by accident, unintentionally') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you by any chance Samson?

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Извините, а вы случайно не Самсон?
examples.trans: Hello! Excuse me, are you by any chance Samson?

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be able', forming an aspectual pair with 'мочь'.

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.
Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Secondary conversational sense ('exactly, precisely') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

убрать.gloss: to remove, to take away; to tidy up

meanings.en: to remove, to take away, to cut out
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'брать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to remove', forming an aspectual pair with 'убирать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to clean up, to tidy') (a room) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты можешь убрать весь этот шум?
examples.trans: Can you cut out all this noise?
Take the phone off the table.

examples.text: Так, ты можешь убрать весь этот шум? Нам нужен только Аникеев.
examples.trans: Right, can you cut out all this noise? We only need Anikeev.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
